runs.answer_summary: In ripgrep, `Standard::sink` and `Standard::sink_with_path` both initialize the replacement helper with `Replacer::new()`, so the helper's initial state is the same at both sites. The only difference is the `path` field. `Replacer::new()` sets `space: None`, meaning no capture locations or buffers exist until the first replacement allocates them.

runs.answer_summary: Both Standard construction sites initialize the replacer the same way: `Replacer::new()`, which returns `Replacer { space: None }`. runs.answer_summary: Ky decides whether the caller supplied Content-Type in the Ky constructor with one predicate, at source/core/Ky.ts:525: `const userProvidedContentType = options.headers !== undefined && mergeHeaders({}, options.headers).has('content-type');`. It is true only when `options.headers` is defined and, after normalization, contains a content-type entry. The only header input consulted is `options.headers`. The Request input's headers are deliberately excluded (Ky.ts:524 comment). The predicate gates two writes: the JSON default at Ky.ts:527-532 (`content-type: application/json` is set only when `!userProvidedContentType`), and the deletion of an inherited content-type at Ky.ts:536-542 (only when the input is a Request, the body is FormData or URLSearchParams, and `!userProvidedContentType`). The init-hook ordering is now confirmed: Ky.create clones options for init hooks (Ky.ts:350-351), runs them synchronously (Ky.ts:353-355), then calls `new Ky(input, initHookOptions)` (Ky.ts:357), so the predicate sees headers after init-hook changes.

runs.answer_summary: Ky decides whether the user supplied Content-Type with one predicate in the Ky constructor: `options.headers !== undefined && mergeHeaders({}, options.headers).has('content-type')` (source/core/Ky.ts:525). The only header input it consults is the caller's `options.headers`. A Content-Type on a `Request` input does not count, because the input's headers are merged into `#options.headers` separately and the predicate never reads `input.headers`. The predicate is true only when `options.headers` is defined and, after normalization through `Headers` and the deletion-marker handling in `mergeHeaders`, still contains `content-type`. The flag is consumed in the same constructor: it suppresses the default `content-type: application/json` for `json` bodies, and it suppresses the deletion of `content-type` when a Request input is rebuilt with FormData or URLSearchParams bodies.

runs.answer_summary: When the argument count is wrong, ExactArgs returns an error and the command's Run is never called. The error reads `accepts N arg(s), received M`, where N is the expected count and M is the actual count. Validation runs before Run. Existing test TestExactArgs_WithInvalidCount calls ExactArgs(2) with three args ("a", "b", "c") and asserts the message `accepts 2 arg(s), received 3`.

runs.answer_summary: ExactArgs(n) returns a validator that rejects any argument count other than n. It returns the error `accepts %d arg(s), received %d` with the expected and actual counts. Cobra's test suite covers this with TestExactArgs_WithInvalidCount: ExactArgs(2) given 3 args must yield `accepts 2 arg(s), received 3`. I did not trace command.go to confirm that the handler is skipped on error; that is inferred from the validator's return value, not read.

runs.answer_summary: ExactArgs(n) rejects any positional-argument count other than n. It returns an error and the command's Run is never called. The error text is "accepts N arg(s), received M". Existing test TestExactArgs_WithInvalidCount calls ExactArgs(2) with three args ("a", "b", "c") and expects exactly "accepts 2 arg(s), received 3".

Ky decides whether the user supplied Content-Type in the `Ky` constructor, using only the caller's `options.headers`, never the `input` Request's headers. The predicate is `options.headers !== undefined && mergeHeaders({}, options.headers).has('content-type')` (source/core/Ky.ts:525). Only the `options.headers` value is consulted. Its result gates two later decisions: whether a `json` body sets `application/json`, and whether a Request-input FormData/URLSearchParams body drops the inherited Content-Type.

Ky decides whether the caller supplied a Content-Type with one predicate that reads only the caller's `options.headers`. It does not read a Request input's headers. The predicate is `options.headers !== undefined && mergeHeaders({}, options.headers).has('content-type')` (source/core/Ky.ts:524-525). It is true only when `options.headers` is defined and, after normalization, contains a content-type entry. `Headers.has` is case-insensitive. A `'content-type': undefined` entry is treated as not supplied, because `mergeHeaders` deletes keys whose value is `undefined`.

Both Standard sink constructors initialize the replacer identically with Replacer::new(), which returns Replacer { space: None }. The path argument changes only the sink's `path` field (None vs Some(PrinterPath)), not the replacer. The no-path constructor, Standard::sink, calls Replacer::new() directly. The path constructor, Standard::sink_with_path, first delegates to sink() when config.path is false, and otherwise calls Replacer::new() in the same way. The helper's initial state has no Space allocated.

Both `StandardSink` construction sites initialize the replacement helper identically: `replacer: Replacer::new()`. The path argument only affects the separate `path` field. `Replacer::new()` allocates nothing. Its internal `space` is `None`, and the capture, destination and match buffers are created lazily on the first replacement. Both sites build the sink with the same `Replacer::new()` call; the only difference is the `path` field. `sink_with_path` also returns early to `sink()` when path printing is disabled, so that case gets the same no-path state.
